text:
anna: quick heads-up — bringing up raven-3b-int8 on canary for func_call/JSON compliance tests :eyeglasses:
anna: seeing intermittent schema failures where arrays get serialized as strings inside the func_call payload (e.g. "items": "[... ]")
anna: repro attached below, pretty deterministic on short list outputs but only after 40-80 tokens. curious if quantization changed tokenization boundaries or eos handling
jordan: can you paste the failing outputs and the expected shape?
anna: expected: {
  "action": "create_order",
  "params": {
    "items": [ {"sku": "A1", "qty": 2}, {"sku": "B2", "qty": 1} ],
    "priority": "normal"
  }
}
anna: observed: {
  "action": "create_order",
  "params": {
    "items": "[{"sku": "A1", "qty": 2}, {"sku": "B2", "qty": 1}]",
    "priority": "normal"
  }
}
liam: hmm that smells like tokenization joining quote tokens or a missing comma escape at generation boundaries
liam: could also be our postprocessor running stringify on nested sequences when kv-cache boundary is hit
anna: repro command I used: 
```
# run local canary request
curl -sS -X POST https://canary.redwood/api/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TEST' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"raven-3b-int8","prompt":"You are an order agent. Return a func_call with action and params JSON. Items is a list of sku/qty pairs.","max_tokens":120,"temperature":0.0,"function_call":{"name":"create_order","arguments_schema":{...}}}'
```
anna: output sample in log: 
```
FUNC_CALL: create_order
ARGS:
{"action":"create_order","params":{"items":"[{"sku": "A1", "qty": 2}]","priority":"normal"}}
```
jordan: thanks. can you run mirror-replica (same prompt) on fp16 and compare? if fp16 emits correct arrays, likely quantization side-effect
anna: ran fp16 -> clean arrays, consistent. int8 fails ~12% of runs across 1000 samples
liam: what's the token boundary where it flips? do you have tokenized view?
anna: yes i captured tokens around the items start: 
```
... "items" :  "["    "{"sku":"   " "A1" ,"  " "qty": 2"  "]"  ","  "\n"
```
liam: aha looks like model emitted opening bracket token as separate literal but then later collapsed into a single quoted string token sequence — could be our detokenizer quoting heuristic when a run of punctuation is emitted and the model prefers a token like '"[{' which then downstream gets escaped as text
jordan: we should test two hypotheses: (1) detokenizer/escape layer is overzealous for int8 logits, (2) KV cache boundary triggers a different sampling behavior.
anna: plan: 1) run detokenize-only ablation on int8 (no postprocessor escapes) 2) try forced-prefix with explicit '[' token to bias generation 3) run kv-cache flush to force fresh context and compare
anna: quick results: detokenize-only ablation reduces failures to 4%, forced-prefix to 1.2%, kv-cache flush no change
liam: that points to postprocessor escaping being too aggressive for int8 trajectories
liam: can you capture logits around the punctuation tokens and push to s3? I'll write a tiny analyzer to compare token probs between fp16/int8
anna: uploading now -> s3://redwood-ci/raven3b-int8/logits/2365001234/
deploy-bot: Canary deployment raven-3b-int8 v0.2 rolled at 2026-03-18T15:22:10Z :rocket:
jordan: thanks, next steps: - liam to run detokenizer diff + upload diff artifact - anna to add forced-prefix canary flag for toolcall routes - i'll schedule a 30m sync tomorrow to decide if we roll back or patch postprocessor
liam: i'll post analyzer link once ready (ETA 2h)
anna: tagging here for visibility @jordan @liam :thinking_face: if forced-prefix works we can gate canary with a quick heuristic until we fix postprocessor
anna: any objections?
jordan: no objections, proceed. :thumbsup:
anna: I'll open a lightweight eval run to measure functional correctness delta and include regression alert if >1% failure in production canary.
